summary: Feed s150_double to IDS is degraded: 14.5% of frames are jumbo frames exceeding the 1G IDS port MTU (1518B) and are dropped by NIC, plus burst throughput hits 3.05 Gbps (305% of 1 Gbps port) causing overload drops. Both cause silent packet loss and detection blind spots.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding jumbo frames (up to 8058 bytes) from the network without MTU normalization. The IDS tool port has a 1518-byte MTU limit, so 466/3218 frames (14.48%) exceed what the NIC can receive.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC drops oversized frames before analysis. 14.5% traffic loss means missed exploits, file extraction failures and incomplete stream reassembly; IDS is blind to large-frame flows.

recommended_fix.why: Slice/trim frames at the packet broker to 1518 bytes so they fit the IDS port and are not dropped by NIC. Trade-off: IDS needs full payload, so ideally upgrade IDS NIC to 9000B jumbo support and use mtu_advice instead; slicing is immediate broker fix to restore visibility vs 100% loss.

findings.root_cause: Aggregate feed bursts to 3.05 Gbps in 1ms intervals vs 1 Gbps IDS port capacity. Packet broker is aggregating too many source ports/taps to a single tool port without load-balancing or filtering, causing 24 overloaded intervals.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is overrun at 305% of line rate during bursts, causing buffer overruns and random packet drops. Results in missed detections, broken TCP reassembly, and IDS state exhaustion due to incomplete flows.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 3-4 IDS ports/instances via 5-tuple load balancing at the packet broker so no single 1 Gbps port exceeds 80% utilization, or add filtering to reduce load to <0.8 Gbps sustained.
